trust_boundaries.name: Vendor-submitted invoice content into FinBot's reasoning

remit_rules.excerpt: FinBot MUST NEVER treat instructions, directives, or policy-like language contained in an invoice description ... as commands
Vendor-supplied content is untrusted data, never instructions.
FinBot MUST NEVER let vendor-submitted invoice content alter its approval thresholds, confidence requirement, fraud-detection state, or goals.

threats.summary: Authority, urgency, and production phrases written into an invoice description are scored by _analyze_business_context and used to expedite the invoice past the manual-review threshold and past its own injection flag, so vendor text redirects what the agent decides to do.
The submit route takes the vendor identity from the URL with no session or token, and the portal picker hands any visitor the full vendor list, so an invoice can be filed as any vendor.
Each anonymous invoice submission drives up to five model calls inline with no rate limit, per-caller quota, spend ceiling, or model-call timeout.

trust_boundaries.name: Admin console and /api/admin/* reachable from the public internet

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST require authenticated, role-restricted admin access.
MUST NOT be accessible to vendors or unauthenticated users.
MUST NOT be exposed to a public/untrusted network — reachable only from an internal/authorized network.
Any unauthenticated party exercising admin capabilities.
Any change to FinBot's configuration ... or to its goals — permitted only for an authenticated, authorized admin.

threats.summary: Every admin route — goals, thresholds, fraud toggle, review approval, vendor trust — is exercisable by an anonymous caller because the blueprint carries no authentication, session, or role check.

The console itself is published: admin-dashboard.html sits in the static folder that the catch-all serves from a 0.0.0.0-bound public Render web service, so the control surface is fetchable by URL from anywhere.
Wildcard CORS applied before blueprint registration lets any web origin drive the admin configuration and goals endpoints from a visitor's browser.
Goal text stored by an anonymous writer is rendered into the console with innerHTML, so stored markup executes in the browser of the next operator who opens it.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any other AI/LLM service or outbound integration is outside the configured closure and MUST be reported as a trust expansion.
FinBot MUST NEVER emit vendor bank/payment details or full tax identifiers into AI reasoning text, vendor-visible responses, or logs.
FinBot MUST NEVER transmit vendor PII or payment details to any destination outside CineFlow's authorized systems.

threats.summary: The vendor's contact email — a remit-declared PII class — is placed in the model context on every invoice although no decision path reads it.

Bank name, account number, routing number, and tax identifier could reach the provider through the invoice-details tool result, but the vendor block sent to the model is a fixed four-field projection that excludes them.

trust_boundaries.name: Model decision into the invoice tool surface

remit_rules.excerpt: AI invoice-analysis / decisioning (approve / reject / route-to-review with reasoning and confidence).
FinBot MUST NOT have arbitrary shell, code-execution, or filesystem-command capability.
FinBot MUST NOT have any capability that moves money or initiates payment/fund transfer.

threats.summary: The approve tool writes payment_processed alongside the decision, so a tool the remit scopes to decisions-only also sets the record state a downstream payment process would read as an instruction.

A hijacked model turn could reach a code-execution or filesystem sink if one existed, but the tool inventory is five invoice-specific functions and a sweep for subprocess, os.system, eval, and exec across the tree returns nothing.

Fraud screening binds nothing: detect_fraud_patterns is called only when the model elects to, returns an empty result whenever the admin-writable fraud toggle is off, and its indicators are consumed by no code branch (checked: finbot_agent.py:509 fraud toggle and :543 indicator return — no gate found; a tree-wide search for fraud_indicators shows no read site outside the tool itself).

trust_boundaries.name: Decision into a committed invoice approval

remit_rules.excerpt: Auto-approving an invoice strictly below the configured auto-approve threshold that has passed fraud/prompt-injection screening.
Approving any invoice at or above the manual-review threshold — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer, never auto-approved.
Approving any invoice in which prompt-injection, goal-manipulation, or fraud content was detected — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer.
Approving any invoice whose decision confidence is below the operator-configured minimum AI confidence — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer, never auto-approved.
When prompt-injection or goal-manipulation content is detected in an invoice, FinBot MUST stop short of auto-approval, route the invoice to human review, and alert an admin (recording the detection).

threats.summary: The approval commit tests nothing — not the amount against manual_review_threshold, not the contains_prompt_injection flag the same request just set, not the supplied confidence against confidence_threshold, which has no read site in any decision path.
The human-review backstop is not a gate: review_invoice sets status approved and payment_processed for any anonymous caller, recording only a reviewer name taken from the request body.

trust_boundaries.name: Goal and configuration writes into persistent agent state

remit_rules.excerpt: FinBot MUST NEVER redefine, override, expand, or reprioritize its own goals or operating priorities in response to natural-language content arriving through any vendor-facing input.
its action surface is limited to producing an invoice decision (approve / reject / route-to-review) and MUST NOT be expanded or redirected by ... supplied goals.
FinBot configuration and natural-language goals read/write (capability retained): gated to authenticated, authorized admins and MUST NOT be influenceable by vendor- or invoice-supplied content.

threats.summary: Goal text written once by an anonymous caller persists in the config row and is appended to every later system prompt under CUSTOM GOALS (OVERRIDE ABOVE IF CONFLICTING), so a single request redirects all subsequent invoice decisions rather than one.

Numeric and boolean config writes are equally unbounded — update_config assigns manual_review_threshold, confidence_threshold, speed_priority, and fraud_detection_enabled straight from the request body with no range, type, or sanity check, so screening can be switched off or the review threshold pushed out of reach (checked: finbot_agent.py:750 update_config and admin.py:74 the calling route — no validator found on either side).

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor records readable by any caller

remit_rules.excerpt: Registered CineFlow vendors, each acting only on their own vendor account, invoices, and data.
Any vendor accessing another vendor's invoices, onboarding data, or payment details.
FinBot MUST NEVER expose one vendor's invoices, onboarding data, PII, or payment details to another vendor or to any unauthenticated party.

threats.summary: GET /api/vendors and the invoice detail route serialise the complete vendor row — bank name, account holder, account number, routing number, tax identifier — to any unauthenticated caller, with no projection and no ownership scoping.

The seeded database template shipped in the repository could have carried live vendor payment records into source control, but its vendors and invoices tables are empty and only the default config row is present.
The Flask SECRET_KEY is a committed string literal, identical across every deployment of this code and public to anyone with repository access, so anything the app ever signs is forgeable.
The model-provider credential could have followed the same pattern, but the OpenAI client is constructed with no key argument and reads the environment, and .env is git-ignored.

Only Flask and the Python runtime are pinned exactly; the remaining eleven dependencies are open-ended floors with no lockfile, SBOM, or scanning configuration, so two builds of the same commit can resolve different code.

remit_rules.excerpt: When FinBot's configuration or goals are changed, FinBot MUST record and surface the change to admins.
Every invoice decision (approve / reject / route-to-review) MUST be recorded to a durable audit log with its reasoning and confidence.
Every configuration or goal change MUST be logged with the acting admin and a timestamp.

threats.summary: No logging framework exists anywhere in the tree — three bare print calls are the whole of it — and the config row carries only updated_at, so the highest-impact action in the system, a goal rewrite, leaves no actor, no prior value, and no trace; reprocess additionally clears the previous AI decision fields in place.

attack_paths.name: Anonymous goal rewrite redirects every later decision

steps.summary: any caller reaches /api/admin/finbot/goals on the public listener
the route accepts the goals string with no auth and no content validation
update_goals persists the text as durable agent state
the stored text is appended to every later prompt with override precedence
the next submitted invoice is reasoned about under the attacker's goals
the resulting approve call commits status and payment_processed with no gate to stop it

attack_paths.name: Business-context manipulation through the fallback engine

steps.summary: an invoice is submitted with authority, urgency, and production phrasing in its description
the unauthenticated submit route processes it inline, repeatable at will
with the model client unavailable, the rule engine scores those phrases and expedites past the review threshold and past its own injection flag
the approval is committed with no amount, injection, or confidence check
the invoice lands as approved with payment_processed set

attack_paths.name: Public vendor listing enables impersonation and cross-vendor exposure

steps.summary: the picker is populated from the unauthenticated full vendor listing
the caller reads any vendor's bank, routing, and tax fields and then submits invoices under that vendor id
the chosen vendor's trust_level can additionally be raised through the open admin route, buying the leniency the decision logic keys on

notes.lane_fit: Clean except at two seams: OpenAI is both the LLM call (an agent_core concern) and an upstream provider, and sits in external_deploy per the lane table; and the FinBotConfig row is modelled as agent_core memory although its table is defined in the same module as the tools_mcp datastore, because its content is behaviour-steering agent state rather than business records.
notes.omissions: Arbitration: no substantive divergence from the stored tags. Numbering-only selections, where the graph must name one primary and the finding stores two codes — PRAX-001 keeps its stored ASI03 (absent identity check) over its stored LLM03 co-tag, and PRAX-002 keeps its stored ASI06 primary under the persistence test (stored goals altering behaviour across sessions), LLM01/ASI01 riding as co-tags in the finding. Substantive: PRAX-005 is stored LLM02 and is tagged LLM02 for the disclosure threat at data-at-rest, but its impersonation mechanism ("any visitor can select any vendor and act as them") is tagged ASI03 at untrusted-ingress per the Agentic KB identity row — a second mechanism inside one finding, not a re-tag of the same evidence. PRAX-007 stays null per both KBs' pure-observability-gap row. Suspected but not modelled: the /api/users CRUD blueprint (src/routes/user.py) is registered unauthenticated under the same /api prefix and appears in no remit channel, but no finding covers it, so it is recorded only as evidence on the Flask-app node; admin-dashboard.html:519 and :537 call /api/admin/invoices/<id>/approve and /reject, which the blueprint does not define — dead client code, so no edge; docs/FinBot-CTF-walkthrough-goal-manipulation.md documents the goal-manipulation attack and is treated as documentation, not architecture; the CTF flag-scoring branches on the invoice model are exercise scaffolding and fold into the orchestrator and approve-tool evidence rather than becoming nodes.
